The second heading repeats the open C, paired tall l strokes and i dot; its separate numeral has a curved upper hook and curled lower foot, giving 2.
The diagonal margin text has a tall crossed T, a small raised accent in Théorie and a separate i mark; after the looped de, the surname begins with a large R loop and ends in a short zigzag z.
The heavy initial R loop is followed by connected low arches and a descending q loop; the separate terminal has the same hooked top and curled foot as the nearby heading numeral 2.
A short upper horizontal stroke and oblique middle survive, but a dark cancellation loop closes over the lower body; the uncanceled sigma contours cannot be separated securely.

The first line preserves a deep v-like fork, a partly merged low mark to its right, and a later descending loop. The crossing horizontal strokes cover the subscript and most of the proposed word, so the full phrase remains uncertain.

The prefix and middle remain covered by broad cancellation loops, so no letters in ortho are independently secured. At the right a long descending loop is followed by small fragments and a raised cross-shaped terminal, compatible with abbreviated g plus raised t; separate onal bodies are not recoverable, and the crossing stroke could contribute to the apparent t.

An initial p descender and a later g descender protrude through the long strike, but the two long words and their plural endings are obscured. The final de and rang retain the tall d, low joined letters and final descending g.

The small word has an open upper curl, a long flat exit and a detached terminal mark. A tall stroke from the neighboring line meets its left body, and neither a clear second letter nor a secure grave accent is distinguishable.
A separate shallow v is followed at lower right by the small n strokes; the following word ends in a tall crossed t after a low e/s connection.

The initial p and the later j have distinct descending strokes, but the final letters are compressed into a flat run intersected by the horizontal line. No separate ion or eur ending can be distinguished.
The inserted word shows a tall initial h, a closed e loop, low r/m humps and a crossed t with a separate following i dot; the final en runs out horizontally.
The short word has an angular double bend for s and a short rightward i stroke with a detached dot above it.
The small elevated letter has a descending entry that turns through one rounded trough into a long rightward exit; there is no additional baseline letter.
The lower word starts with a tall h and low e/r run; its final group has a crossed t, a distinct following i mark and a long joined en ending, as in the nearby inserted occurrence.
The diagonal deletion crosses the initial s/o bodies, but a small rounded o remnant, the detached i dot and the separate final t upright and crossbar remain visible.

Between two absolute-value bars are a T/r group, first descending p with a low n, a low u, and a second descending p. The second low index intersects the diagonal deletion and the following equality is crossed through, leaving those two details uncertain.
A triangular initial loop and short vertical survive, but the central bodies and terminal capital are overwritten by dense cancellation; the supposed m and E cannot be separated securely.
The tall initial loop and a few descenders remain above and below the horizontal strike; most intervening small letters and any accents have merged into it.
The opening angular E and low joining stroke precede two tall f stems; the last upright with rightward return survives the horizontal cancellation.
A tiny opening remnant and a later descending stem survive, but the broad horizontal strike covers the word bodies, including the proposed O/n and eu joins.
Small dotted and tall strokes are visible below the preceding formula; the long cancellation and overlapping insertion prevent separating the supposed suffit and de bodies.
A broad looped initial S is followed by a smaller o loop, a short i stroke with its displaced dot, and a long terminal t stroke; the large deletion curve passes below and through the end.
The small label has a compact double trough, but the high rightmost stroke touches its body; it does not supply the detached prime visible at M0846.

A closed O is followed by one short curved falling stroke without a separate feature that distinguishes r from a compressed n. The second word has a dotted i and crossed terminal t, and the gap before w′ contains no extra si.
The short group at the right edge preserves an upright and hooked body, but a large diagonal and horizontal cancellation cover the connection and the proposed final e.
Both outer bars, the capped T and small r, and one double-troughed w are distinct; two short strokes form the terminal equals sign.
A double-troughed w has a separate short raised prime at its upper right, followed by two parallel horizontal strokes.

After rho with its small lower-right index, the parenthesized group has two descending p stems with low n strokes, separated by one compact w body; the closing parenthesis remains visible despite cancellation.

Two short vertical strokes remain at the left, but a horizontal strike merges the middle letters and the right-hand marks. A p, its n, and two closing norm bars cannot all be individually distinguished.
The initial w has two clear low troughs; nearly all subsequent small bodies lie on the heavy cancellation, leaving isolated dots and hooks insufficient to recover the rest.
The first tall d loop, apostrophe-like dot, later l upright, dotted stems and final t survive; the central joins and accents are crossed through and do not securely establish the whole phrase.

A short arch above sigma and compact dot/stroke below are compatible with n and 1 but lack their discriminating detail. The rho loop and descent are clear; its index and following cursive groups remain too compressed to establish i or dans, while the separated parentheses are visibly empty.
In the rotated margin the first word has an open e-like curl and flattened connected ending; after a clear gap the second has a low u/n/e sequence beneath the inserted conséquence.
A low loop rises into a tall d ascender, followed by a connected low u-shaped exit before the separate underlined lemme.

A crossing stroke runs through the initial loop and low connected letter bodies, establishing deletion. Several internal bodies and the proposed acute accent are merged with that stroke, so the word itself remains uncertain.
Inside the rho parentheses the argument has two joined low troughs with a raised middle turn, wider than the single-cup v visible earlier in the same formula.
Between the parentheses are two separate horizontal strokes on the same level, with a visible gap between them and no letter bodies.

An initial short open stroke and small loop lead into a long flattened connected body, with a dot near the final rise. The terminal letters and potential q descent merge with a large crossing stroke, preventing a secure full reading.
Below the inserted atteinte, the deleted body retains a small initial mark, a tall looped stroke, and a terminal small rise. The heavy horizontal cancellation conceals the middle letter sequence.
The one raised character above the summation has a peaked shoulder and short down-and-up exit; it has no paired closed lobes of an infinity sign.

One tall looped f stands beneath its bar, and its separate lower-right index has a long descending hooked return. The hook extends well below the f crossbar and distinguishes j from the dotted i indices in the next line.

The retraced baseline body preserves one upper loop and right exit of e; beneath its right side is a deep hooked lower component. That component extends far below the baseline, like the clear e_j in the next line, rather than stopping at a short i mark.
The crossed-out word has two surviving tall strokes and a low terminal hump/exit. The horizontal cancellation fuses its middle rounded letters, so the full alors sequence is not independently clear.
Immediately to the lower right of the single rho body is a compact dot-like index. There is no descending shaft or hook, unlike the j beneath the adjacent sum.
After the barred e, the alleged index merges with the letter's right exit as a short terminal downstroke. No separate dot or complete lower hook remains to distinguish i from j securely.
One baseline e loop is followed at lower right by a thick descender with a hooked lower return and a dot above it. The deep return identifies j despite the retracing.
